data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note reports results from the Survey of Adult Skills 2023 for Denmark, covering adults aged 16–65 in the 2022–23 cycle (Denmark’s second participation; first in 2011–12). The assessment measures three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—administered exclusively on digital tablets, with proficiency estimated on 500-point scales and mapped to discrete proficiency levels (e.g., Level 1 or below; Levels 4–5). Denmark’s mean performance is above the OECD average in all three domains, with reported shares at low and high proficiency levels (e.g., 18% at Level 1 or below in literacy; 15% at Levels 4–5). The note also documents subgroup differences (e.g., lower proficiency among older adults) and trends over time (literacy and numeracy improved from 2011–12 to 2022–23, while low performance remained stable). It further links higher numeracy proficiency to better labour-force participation and higher wages, and to higher life satisfaction, health, political efficacy, trust, and volunteering, while excluding doorstep-only respondents from some outcome comparisons.
